Vague

VAYG — rhymes with 'plague'; vague directions plague lost travelers. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Vague is not clearly expressed or understood; lacking definite detail.

His directions were so vague that we ended up on the wrong side of town.

Worked Example

You ask a friend where the party is. She says, 'Somewhere downtown, near some restaurant, I think, around eight-ish?' You hang up knowing no more than when you called.

An answer too fuzzy and detail-free to act on is vague. Unlike 'wrong,' vague information isn't necessarily false — it's just too unclear to be useful.

How Vague Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unclear

unclear: not easy to understand

hazy

hazy: indistinct, like something seen through fog

imprecise

imprecise: not exact or specific

Antonyms

precise

precise: exact and accurate

specific

specific: clearly and definitely stated

How Strong Is It? — general → incomprehensible → vague

general vs. vague

general vs. vague: General is weaker than vague — a general answer is broad but still understandable, while a vague one is too unclear to pin down at all.

incomprehensible vs. vague

incomprehensible vs. vague: Incomprehensible is stronger than vague: a vague statement gives you a fuzzy idea, but an incomprehensible one gives you nothing to understand whatsoever.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Vague comes straight from Latin vagus, 'wandering' -- a vague statement wanders around the point instead of landing on it, leaving its meaning drifting and unclear. The same wandering root hides in vagrant and vagabond.

Use the root in a new word: vagabond

Use the root in a new word: vagabond: The vagabond wandered from town to town with everything he owned in one bag.
